one_liner: Discord has a self-serve REST and Gateway API with bot tokens and OAuth2. Discord also hosts an official docs-only MCP server, and community MCP servers cover the live API.
auth_notes: The reference lists three methods: a bot token, an OAuth2 bearer token, and Basic auth. Basic uses client_id:client_secret and only works on OAuth2 token endpoints. OAuth2 is the right choice for multi-user access, and bot tokens suit single-bot use.
access_notes: Anyone can register a developer application and get a client ID, client secret and bot token. Apps with fewer than 10,000 users can enable Privileged Intents in the Developer Portal. Some scopes are limited to approved partners. The pages never use the word 'free', so confidence is medium.
blocker_notes: Minor friction only. Apps with 10,000 or more users need approval for Privileged Intents, and some scopes are partner-only. Neither blocks a toolkit.

evidence.quote: We support the authorization code grant, the implicit grant, client credentials, and some modified special-for-Discord flows for Bots and Webhooks.
